📚 Today you learned

Naked / Unprotected Positions

A "naked" position isn't a strategy — it's a filled order nobody followed up on. GOOG is the live example: the GTC buy limit at $365 sat quietly for weeks, filled somewhere below that level, and nobody attached a stop because the fill happened silently and portfolio.json was never resynced. In forex you'd never leave a filled order unhedged for three weeks — the discipline there is usually tighter because platforms surface open positions constantly. US equity brokers (IBKR included) don't push that at you the same way; a GTC fill just sits in your positions list until you check. The fix isn't a smarter order type, it's a habit: every time you place a GTC entry, calendar a same-day check once it's plausible the price crossed your limit, and never let more than a day pass without confirming your live position list matches what your tracking sheet says.

Also today: Position reconciliation — the practice of matching your broker's live account state against your own tracking record on a fixed cadence, catching exactly this kind of drift before it compounds.
